customers.intro: Customers group devices by the business you support — assign a device to one from its Overview tab. A customer number is just a free-text reference for your own records (invoicing, ticketing system, etc.), not validated against anything.
customers.title: Customers
customers.groupsHint: Devices and alert rules can be scoped to a group instead of (or within) a customer — assign a device to one from its Overview tab. A group left without a customer applies across all customers.

alerts.intro: Alerts fire automatically when a rule's condition is met (e.g. CPU above a threshold, a service stopped, a device gone offline). "Open" needs attention; "acknowledged" means someone's seen it but it isn't fixed yet; "resolved" clears it from the active list.
alerts.rulesHint: Rules are evaluated continuously against every device in their scope. Disabling a rule stops new alerts from it without deleting it.
alerts.title: Alerts

users.intro: Dashboard accounts for your own staff — separate from the per-device remote-support account, and separate from customer logins (there are none: customers never get dashboard access).
users.roleReadOnlyHint: Can view devices, customers and monitoring/maintenance history — no remote access, no changes.
users.roleTechnicianHint: Day-to-day remote maintenance: terminal, SSH/RDP tunnels, file access, service/process control, maintenance notes.
users.roleAdminHint: Everything technician has, plus customer/alert/settings management — but not user or role management.
users.roleSuperAdminHint: Full access, including creating/managing other users and roles. Grant sparingly.
users.sessionsRevoked: All sessions for this user were revoked.
users.title: Users
users.mfaHint: MFA required is per-user. The server also has a global default (<0>admin.require_mfa</0> in server.yaml) — if that is <1>true</1>, MFA is enforced regardless of this checkbox; both must be off for a user to skip MFA entirely.
users.createdHint: User "{{username}}" created — this password is shown only once, copy it now:
users.createdMfaHint: MFA setup will be required the first time they log in.

releases.title: Agent Releases
releases.hint: Release artifacts are signed offline with <0>wr-release-sign</0> — this server never holds a production signing key. Submissions are verified against the configured trusted public key (<1>WR_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY_FILE</1>) before being accepted. GitHub sync (below) reads the .sha256/.sig sidecar files wr-release-sign writes alongside each artifact — upload all three as release assets and the same verification applies automatically.
releases.manualHint: For a one-off release, or if you're not using GitHub sync. Fill in exactly what wr-release-sign printed for this artifact.

networkUsage.title: Network usage
networkUsage.hint: Which devices are using the most bandwidth, ranked by total traffic. "To server" is just this agent's own control-channel overhead — everything else on this device's network is "total". Based on raw samples, so an overly long window may miss devices' older history once it's past the configured raw retention (Settings → Network traffic history retention).
networkUsage.noData: No network traffic data in this window yet.

help.selectTopic: Select a topic on the left.

appearance.title: Theme & layout
appearance.hint: Purely visual — stored in this browser only, nothing is sent to the server.

retention.title: Monitoring history retention
retention.hint: How long raw (high-resolution) and hourly-averaged CPU/RAM/disk history is kept before being deleted. Alerts are not affected by this — they're kept indefinitely until manually acknowledged/resolved/deleted.

networkRetention.title: Network traffic history retention
networkRetention.hint: Same idea, but for network traffic history specifically — it's collected far more often (roughly once a minute per device, buffered locally on the agent and uploaded in batches) than CPU/RAM/disk, so it gets its own, shorter default raw retention to keep the row volume reasonable; the hourly rollup still covers the long term.

rotation.title: Remote-support account rotation
rotation.hint: Automatically generates and applies a new password for the "remotewartung" account on every device on a schedule — it's machine-generated and never seen by anyone, so unlike a human login password there's no downside to rotating it, only upside: it limits how long a copy would stay useful if the database were ever compromised. Set to 0 to disable (the default — rotation still works on demand from a device's Remote tab either way).

telegram.title: Telegram alert notifications
telegram.hint: Sends a Telegram message every time a new alert opens (docs/TODO.md lists email/ntfy/webhooks as possible future channels — Telegram is the first one built). Setup:
telegram.step1: In Telegram, message <0>@BotFather</0>, send <1>/newbot</1>, and follow the prompts. It gives you a bot token like 123456:ABC-DEF1234...
telegram.step2: Message your new bot directly (or add it to a group and mention it once) so it can see the chat.
telegram.step3: Open <0>https://api.telegram.org/bot<YOUR_TOKEN>/getUpdates</0> in a browser (replace <1><YOUR_TOKEN></1>) and find <2>"chat":{"id":...}</2> in the response — that number is your chat ID.
telegram.step4: Paste both below, save, then send a test message to confirm it works.
telegram.currentlyConfigured: Currently configured (chat ID {{chatId}}, last set {{updatedAt}}). Enter a new bot token below only if you want to replace it.
telegram.testSent: Test message sent — check your Telegram chat.

audit.title: Audit log integrity
audit.hint: Every audit entry is cryptographically chained to the one before it, so an entry can't be edited or deleted afterwards without breaking the chain from that point on — this recomputes the whole chain from scratch and checks it against what's stored. Read-only, but scans the entire audit log, so it's a manual action rather than something run on every page load.
audit.chainIntact_one: Chain intact — {{count}} entry checked, no tampering detected.
audit.chainIntact_other: Chain intact — {{count}} entries checked, no tampering detected.
audit.preChainNote_one: ({{count}} older entry predates this feature and isn't covered by the chain.)
audit.preChainNote_other: ({{count}} older entries predate this feature and aren't covered by the chain.)
audit.chainBroken: Chain broken at entry #{{id}} ({{count}} entries checked before the break was found) — this entry or one before it no longer matches what was originally recorded.

supportCredential.hint: A dedicated local account ("remotewartung") for logging into the SSH/RDP tunnel above — separate from any of the customer's own accounts. Every reveal is audited.

terminalView.title: Terminal
terminalView.hint: A native command-line session in your browser (PowerShell on Windows, the default shell on Linux) — runs as the agent's own account by default. Use "Request Admin Rights" for a time-limited elevated session when you need it.
